findings.title: forEach with async callback causes recurring event calendar deletions to be silently skipped
findings.body: The `forEach(async (credential) => {...})` on line 460 does not await the async callbacks. Since `getCalendar` is now async, the callbacks haven't finished by the time execution reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` on line 652. At that point `apiDeletes` is still empty (or incomplete), so calendar events for recurring bookings are never actually deleted. This should use a `for...of` loop or `Promise.all` with `.map()` to ensure the deletions are collected and awaited.

findings.title: forEach with async callback makes try/catch ineffective
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` on line 125 is wrapped in a try/catch (lines 124-139), but `forEach` does not await the async callbacks. Any error thrown inside the callback (e.g., from `await getCalendar(...)` or `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`) will result in an unhandled promise rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding try/catch. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))` instead.

findings.title: forEach with async callback makes try/catch ineffective
findings.body: Same issue as vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` on line 125 is inside a try/catch that will never catch errors from the async callbacks. Errors from `await getCalendar(...)` or `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` become unhandled promise rejections.

findings.title: forEach with async callback makes calendar/video deletions fire-and-forget
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` on line 553 fires off async calendar and video deletion operations without awaiting them. The function proceeds to send the reschedule email (line 570) before the deletions complete. If a deletion fails, the error is silently lost. This should use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` to ensure deletions complete (or at least errors are handled) before continuing.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials returns Promise in calendar field without being async, breaking the return type contract
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` is a synchronous function that now returns objects where the `calendar` field is `Promise<Calendar | null>` (because `getCalendar` is now async). While `getConnectedCalendars` correctly awaits `item.calendar`, any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that previously accessed `item.calendar` as a resolved `Calendar | null` will now receive a Promise object. This is a subtle breaking change in the function's return type that could cause runtime errors in callers not updated in this PR.

findings.title: All dynamic imports are initiated eagerly at module load time, negating lazy-loading benefits
findings.body: Every `import("./...")` call in the appStore object literal is executed immediately when the module is evaluated. This means all app modules are fetched in parallel at startup rather than on demand. If the goal is to reduce initial bundle size or startup time, the imports should be deferred (e.g., by wrapping them in functions or using a getter pattern) so they are only loaded when actually accessed.
